diagram_source: a sheet titled as a one-line (single-line or power riser) diagram: the equipment it draws is the service and distribution gear
unsized_source: a feeder tagged unsized (XX, TBD) or with a feeder schedule row giving no conductors: the engineer still has to size it
code_size_source: inferred (code): the feeder the one-line leaves unsized is built the way the field sizes it, for the rating of the gear it feeds: the smallest copper whose 75 C ampacity carries it (NEC 215.2(A), 240.4, Table 310.16), its equipment ground by NEC Table 250.122 (never larger than the phase conductors), a neutral with the phases, and the raceway by NEC Chapter 9 fill; the engineer's size replaces it
layout_source: proposed: beside the gear it feeds, in the one-line's order (the plans don't locate it); trade practice sets service gear side by side on one wall

kinds.title: Meter socket
kinds.size_source: trade practice: a typical meter socket up to that rating (height x width x depth in, ringless/ring type), the utility's approved socket governs; mounted at 5 ft to its center (common utility service rules)

kinds.title: CT cabinet
kinds.size_source: trade practice: a typical utility CT cabinet up to that rating (height x width x depth in), to the serving utility's standard

kinds.title: Disconnect switch
kinds.size_source: trade practice: a typical heavy-duty safety switch enclosure up to that rating (height x width x depth in, NEMA 1/3R); its submittal replaces it

kinds.title: Enclosed circuit breaker
kinds.size_source: trade practice: a typical enclosed molded-case breaker up to that frame (height x width x depth in); its submittal replaces it

kinds.title: Wireway (gutter)
kinds.size_source: trade practice: a typical service wireway up to that rating (height x length x depth in, the length along the wall spanning the gear it joins); a size printed on the one-line governs

kinds.title: Switchboard
kinds.size_source: trade practice: a typical front-accessible switchboard section up to that rating (height x width x depth in); its submittal replaces it

kinds.title: Transformer
kinds.size_source: trade practice: a typical ventilated dry-type transformer up to that kVA (height x width x depth in), on a 4 in pad; its submittal replaces it

kinds.title: Lighting contactor
kinds.size_source: trade practice: a typical electrically held lighting contactor in a NEMA 1 enclosure (height x width x depth in)

kinds.title: Time switch
kinds.size_source: trade practice: a typical 7-day astronomical time switch enclosure (height x width x depth in)

kinds.title: Photocell
kinds.size_source: trade practice: a typical exterior photocontrol on a weatherproof box, 10 ft up on the outside wall, facing north

rod_source: trade practice: a 5/8 in x 8 ft copper-clad rod (NEC 250.52(A)(5), 250.53(A)(4): 8 ft in contact with the earth)
ufer_source: NEC 250.52(A)(3): at least 20 ft of bare copper (or rebar) in a footing in contact with the earth
gec_source: NEC Table 250.66: the grounding electrode conductor by the largest service-entrance conductor (copper); a rod's need not be larger than #6, a concrete-encased electrode's than #4 (250.66(A), (B))
panel_size_source: inferred (trade practice): a typical panelboard enclosure for its rating and circuits (manufacturers' standard boxes: 20 in wide and 5.75 in deep up to 400 A); no gear submittal gives its box, which replaces this when one does
